definitions.explanation: The Celsius temperature scale, in which water freezes at 0 degrees and boils at 100 degrees. Japan uses the Celsius scale for all temperature measurements in daily life, weather, and science.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}の{気温|きおん}は{摂氏|せっし}30{度|ど}だ。
{水|みず}は{摂氏|せっし}100{度|ど}で{沸騰|ふっとう}する。
アメリカでは{華氏|かし}が{使|つか}われるが、{日本|にほん}では{摂氏|せっし}が{標準|ひょうじゅん}である。
examples.english: Fahrenheit is used in America, but Celsius is the standard in Japan.

notes:
USAGE:
Named after the Chinese transliteration of Anders Celsius ({摂爾修斯|セルシウス}). In everyday Japanese, temperatures are almost always given in Celsius without explicitly saying {摂氏|せっし} — people simply say 30{度|ど} (30 degrees). The word {摂氏|せっし} is used when explicitly distinguishing from Fahrenheit or in scientific contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {摂氏|せっし}〜{度|ど}: ~ degrees Celsius
- {摂氏|せっし}{温度|おんど}: Celsius temperature

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {華氏|かし}: Fahrenheit (the counterpart scale used in the US)
